title: Senior's toolkit: pytest on the command line
summary: pytest's everyday flags (-k, -x, --lf, -vv, --durations), coverage with pytest-cov, parallel runs with pytest-xdist, and mutation testing with mutmut.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: pytest
steps.body: The flags and plugins that make a Python suite fast to work in.

toolkit.what: The inner loop: rerun what failed last time, stop at the first failure, quiet output.
flags: only the tests that failed last run (--ff: those first, then the rest)

toolkit.what: List the slowest tests: where a suite's minutes go.
flags: the 10 slowest setups, calls and teardowns
turn pytest-randomly's random order off to compare

toolkit.what: Coverage with pytest-cov (coverage.py): the line numbers each file misses.
flags: fail below a threshold (same caveats as in .NET)

toolkit.what: Run tests in parallel worker processes with pytest-xdist; shared-state flakes show up fast.
flags: keep a module's tests on one worker (shared fixtures)

toolkit.what: Mutation testing for Python: mutate the code, run the tests per mutant, list the survivors.
toolkit.example:
mutmut run
mutmut results
mutmut show billing.grade__mutmut_3

steps.prompt: Match the pytest flag to its xUnit/.NET cousin.
Rerun only the failing tests, stop at the first failure, and show full diffs.
steps.explain: `--lf` picks last run's failures, `-x` stops at the first one, `-vv` prints long values in full.
